title: Touring Maine with the Jenkins' Orphanage band
summary: He left with the orphanage show touring Maine in a homemade bus, playing Grange halls in uniform.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: After I got married -- right? Okay. And, we had our kid -- our first kid, I left Charleston. Jenkins' group had a show. They was going to get ready to tour Maine -- the state of Maine. Right?
So, I left there with them. I left there with them, and went up to Maine with this show that they had.
So you went out on the road?

Right. Went out on the road with them, and they had this show. And -- with my banjo. And, we toured the state of Maine, playing in Grange halls -- whatever they had up there in order to accomodate this travelling show, you know. It was something. (laugh)
(laugh)
What did they do about those kids -- I mean, were they payed anything, or just given food?
Listen -- my experience with them -- I didn't know. I don't think they got paid -- I don't know.
They just went out?

They went out to -- and made -- take in, you know, contributions and the like. And, I don't know how the arrangement was made as far as the shows, and the hall, and everybody -- how they were paid off. I don't even remember what I got.
And the proceeds were going out to raise funds for the home.
-- For the home. Yes.
Well, what did they do? Travel in a bus?
Yeah. We had a bus.
Well, how many were --
But, it was one of those homemade bus, you know, that you -- (laugh) -- that you. One of those buses that was made into a bus -- listen, I can't describe it. But anyway, it was very uncomfortable.
Was it -- a truck?

[It] was a truck to carry the equipment and what-not, and we just made a tour of Maine. We used to have to get up around 12 o'clock, and holy you know, all through the streets, and parade, you know. Maine -- we were in all the small towns in Maine.
You had to let them know you were there?
Yeah -- we had to dress -- uniforms that we wore.
How many guys were you?
I don't know if I remember.
I mean it wasn't just -- was it pure brass then? Still? Or did you have saxophones?
No, we had saxophones. We had a reed section.
Oh, you did.

I'm glad you mentioned that. It -- made me remember. We had two altos and one tenor. We had one -- let's see -- one -- two -- I think we had two trumpets, two trombones, one bass -- tuba, in other words.
Two trumpets and two trombones? Four brass?
Yes.
It was a marching band, remember?
And drums.
Nobody played piano?
No, I don't remember any piano player.
No. No. Just --
I don't remember, no -- I don't remember anybody playing -- wait a minute, wait a minute. No, I don't really remember a piano player.
And what -- was your music, stocks?
Huh?
Were you playing stocks? The music that you were playing? Or was it all marching stuff?
I don't remember -- I don't remember any music. As far as the show was concerned -- I don't know whether they had any music or not.
They just had numbers.
Yeah. I don't remember if they had music or not. But, I wanted to go, you know. I wanted experience. I wanted to get on the road.
And did that cinch it as far as you were concerned? Did you know then -- that's it? Did you know -- yeah, that's what you want? Or were you unsure?
Well, I didn't make the conditions of the, you know what I mean? It was something else --
But you -- I mean you wanted to leave to see the world.
I wanted -- yeah. I wanted -- Yeah. I wanted to go.
